ga_bk_crag.blurb: This small, wooded former quarry sits inside metro Atlanta and holds about ten climbs, most of them top-ropes with a few trad lines and a single boulder problem. Grades run from around 5.6 up to 5.10, with most routes landing at 5.9, so it suits beginners and anyone teaching newer climbers. Routes are short and finish at the top of the wall, with anchors often set back on trees. Expect a rough, informal setting with litter, dirt and plenty of ivy, and be aware that the floor floods after rain. The car park is a small pull-in off a residential street.

ga_goose_egg_rock.blurb: A lone, tucked-away boulder in the valley below the main Pine Mountain trail, northwest of Atlanta. Ten problems are packed onto it, spanning V1 up to V6, with a cluster of V6s at the hard end and a spread of easier and middle grades below. Lines include an arete, a shallow roof and tall faces, so bring pads and a spotter, since several finish high. The spot is fairly bright for a valley and a stream runs close by. The stone is brittle after wet weather, so give it a couple of dry days first.

ga_constellation_boulder.blurb: One of the most striking features at Morgan Falls, this is a steep, cliff-like overhang a short uphill scramble above the trail in north Atlanta. Ten boulder problems run from V2 up to V7, with most clustered around V5 and V6, named after stars and constellations. The leftmost side is a shelved overhang with a mix of jugs, slopers and crimps, while the right side is loose and best avoided. The wall is hard to spot from below in spring and summer when foliage fills in, and it would still benefit from more brushing and traffic.

ga_golden_harvest_boulder.blurb: A standout boulder near the centre of the Rocktown field in northwest Georgia, beside a stream on the valley floor. Ten problems cover a wide range, from an easy warm-up around V0 to the hard namesake line at the top end, with a good cluster of V5 to V8 problems in between. The best-known lines are on the far side from where the trail arrives. The rock is sandstone typical of the area, and the trails here are easy to wander off in the moss, so take care finding the way down. Best in the cooler months, when the sandstone is at its grippiest.

ga_sherman_roof.blurb: A compact, heavily chalked roof at Rocktown in northwest Georgia, reached by following the main trail past the Orb and the front corridor. It holds ten sandstone problems from V1 to V9, but the reputation rests on the hard roof lines in the V6 to V8 range, plus a harder traverse. A few easy problems at V1 give lower-grade climbers something to try. The best lines are steep and powerful, so pads and a spotter help. Cooler months from autumn through winter give the best friction.

ga_cave_wall.blurb: The tallest and best section of the small Murder Creek boulders in middle Georgia, sitting beside the creek just left of a big round boulder that forms a cave. Around ten problems range from V0 to V4, with a handful at V3, so it suits newer boulderers and those after a quiet, low-key session. The wall is roughly eighteen feet at its highest, holds thin out near the top, and topouts are sloping and covered in dirt and leaves. A worthwhile stop if you are passing through rather than a destination trip. Late fall and winter avoid the heat, bugs and snakes.
